reports.title: Daniel Futers: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The recording of information, particularly that conveyed by telephone, was not as comprehensive as it ought to have been. For example, a record of an altercation had not been made.
Comprehensive planning for home leave and discharge from hospital was not evident, including contingency planning and the involvement of the family.
Overall situational awareness about Daniel was not evident, including the reconciliation of conflicting accounts about him.

reports.title: Brenda Shields: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: Discharge processes to be reviewed by Hadrian Ward to ensure onward referrals are communicated with receiving teams
promises.summary: Review discharge processes to ensure referrals communicated

promises.quote: For the team to continue monitoring and assurance of care giver inclusion in safety planning and discharge planning
promises.summary: Monitor and assure caregiver inclusion in safety and discharge planning

promises.quote: Carer leads continue to roll out carer awareness training

concerns.quote: Brenda was discharged without any planned follow up. Her family were not involved in the discharge process despite assurances that they would be, her GP did not receive discharge notification from the Hadrian unit until 8 days after the event or from the Crisis team until 10 days after Brenda's death. Referrals promised from Hadrian unit to Drug/Alcohol services and Persistent Physical Symptoms Service were not made.

Inadequate weight seems to have been given to Brenda's alcohol problems and her assurances that all was, and would continue to be well were accepted at face value despite her recent history, her family find it hard to understand how she could be graded low risk on the day she died.

I refer you to the PFD report I issued referring to Charlotte Grace on 29/10/19. Assurances were given in response to that report which again focused on discharge without family/carer involvement which is surely paramount. I note actions mentioned in the incident report in this case but am still concerned that similar events may occur in future.
concerns.hazard: repeat of discharge without family involvement
